lemma LogDerivZetaBnd :
    ∃ (A : ℝ) (_ : A ∈ Ioc 0 (1 / 2)) (C : ℝ) (_ : 0 < C), ∀ (σ : ℝ) (t : ℝ) (_ : 3 < |t|)
    (_ : σ ∈ Ico (1 - A / Real.log |t| ^ 9) (1 + A / Real.log |t| ^ 9)), ‖ζ' (σ + t * I) / ζ (σ + t * I)‖ ≤
      C * Real.log |t| ^ 9

    ∃ (A : ℝ) (_ : A ∈ Ioc 0 (1 / 2)) (C : ℝ) (_ : 0 < C), ∀ (σ : ℝ) (t : ℝ) (_ : 3 < |t|)
    (_ : σ ∈ Ico (1 - A / Real.log |t| ^ 9) (1 + A / Real.log |t| ^ 9)), ‖ζ' (σ + t * I) / ζ (σ + t * I)‖ ≤

by
  obtain ⟨A, hA, C, hC, h⟩ := ZetaInvBnd
  obtain ⟨A', hA', C', hC', h'⟩ := ZetaDerivUpperBnd
  use min A A', ⟨lt_min hA.1 hA'.1, min_le_of_right_le hA'.2⟩, C * C', mul_pos hC hC'
  intro σ t t_gt ⟨σ_ge, σ_lt⟩
  have logt_gt : (1 : ℝ) < Real.log |t| := logt_gt_one t_gt.le
  have σ_ge' : 1 - A / Real.log |t| ^ 9 ≤ σ := by
    apply le_trans (tsub_le_tsub_left ?_ 1) σ_ge
    apply div_le_div_of_nonneg_right (min_le_left A A')
    exact pow_nonneg (zero_le_one.trans logt_gt.le) _
  have σ_ge'' : 1 - A' / Real.log |t| ≤ σ := by
    apply le_trans (tsub_le_tsub_left ?_ 1) σ_ge
    apply div_le_div₀ hA'.1.le (min_le_right A A') (lt_trans (by norm_num) logt_gt) ?_
    exact le_self_pow₀ logt_gt.le (by norm_num)
  replace h := h σ t t_gt ⟨σ_ge', by calc
    σ < 1 + min A A' / Real.log |t| ^ 9 := σ_lt
    _ ≤ 1 + A / Real.log |t| ^ 9 := by gcongr; simp⟩
  replace h' := h' σ t t_gt ⟨σ_ge'', by
   calc
    σ ≤ 1 + min A A' / Real.log |t| ^ 9 := by linarith [σ_lt]

    _ ≤ 1 + (1/2) / Real.log |t| ^ 9 := by gcongr; simp [Set.mem_Ioc] at hA' hA ⊢ ; simp [hA.2]

    _ ≤ 1 + (1/2) / 1 := by
          gcongr
          calc
            1 ≤ Real.log |t| := by linarith
            _ ≤ (Real.log |t|)^9 := Real.self_le_rpow_of_one_le (by linarith) (by linarith)
          norm_cast

    _ ≤ 2 := by linarith
    ⟩
  simp only [norm_div]
  convert! mul_le_mul h h' (by simp) ?_ using 1 <;> (norm_cast; ring_nf); positivity

  set s₀ : ℂ := 3 + t * I with hs₀def
  have hsim : s.im = t := by simp [hsdef]
  have hs₀im : s₀.im = t := by simp [hs₀def]
  have hsre : s.re = σ := by simp [hsdef]
  have hs₀re : s₀.re = 3 := by simp [hs₀def]
  have hs1 : s ≠ 1 := by
    intro h; have := congrArg Complex.im h; rw [hsim, Complex.one_im] at this; linarith
  have hs₀1 : s₀ ≠ 1 := by
    intro h; have := congrArg Complex.im h; rw [hs₀im, Complex.one_im] at this; linarith
  have hs0 : s ≠ 0 := by
    intro h; have := congrArg Complex.im h; rw [hsim, Complex.zero_im] at this; linarith
  have hs₀0 : s₀ ≠ 0 := by
    intro h; have := congrArg Complex.im h; rw [hs₀im, Complex.zero_im] at this; linarith
  have hxis : xi s ≠ 0 := by
    intro h
    obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ := exists_xiZeroCopy_of_xi_eq_zero h
    have := hall q
    rw [hq, sub_self, norm_zero] at this
    linarith
  have hxis₀ : xi s₀ ≠ 0 := by
    intro h
    obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ := exists_xiZeroCopy_of_xi_eq_zero h
    have := xiZeroCopy_re_lt_one q
    rw [hq, hs₀re] at this
    linarith
  have hζs : riemannZeta s ≠ 0 := by
    intro h
    apply hxis
    rw [xi_eq_xiUnit_mul_zeta hs0 hs1 (by rw [hsre]; linarith), h, mul_zero]
  have hζs₀ : riemannZeta s₀ ≠ 0 := by
    intro h
    apply hxis₀
    rw [xi_eq_xiUnit_mul_zeta hs₀0 hs₀1 (by rw [hs₀re]; norm_num), h, mul_zero]
  -- the decomposition
  have hdec := logDeriv_zeta_eq_logDeriv_xi (s := s) (by rw [hsre]; linarith) hs1 hζs
  have hdec₀ := logDeriv_zeta_eq_logDeriv_xi (s := s₀) (by rw [hs₀re]; norm_num) hs₀1 hζs₀
  have hpf := logDeriv_xi_sub_eq_tsum hxis hxis₀
  -- the tsum bound
  have hsum : Summable fun q : XiZeroCopy => ‖(s - (q.1 : ℂ))⁻¹ - (s₀ - (q.1 : ℂ))⁻¹‖ :=
    summable_norm_iff.mpr (summable_partialFractionDiff hxis hxis₀)
  have htsum : ‖∑' q : XiZeroCopy, ((s - (q.1 : ℂ))⁻¹ - (s₀ - (q.1 : ℂ))⁻¹)‖
      ≤ (3650 + 5 * smallHeightCount) * Real.log t / δ := by
    refine (norm_tsum_le_tsum_norm hsum).trans ?_
    exact hsum.tsum_le_of_sum_le fun F =>
      sum_norm_partialFractionDiff_le hσ hσ2 ht hδ hδ1 hall F
  -- the boundary terms
  have hz₀ := norm_logDeriv_zeta_three_le t
  have hi₀ := norm_inv_le_quarter hs₀im ht
  have hi₀' : ‖(s₀ - 1)⁻¹‖ ≤ 1 / 4 := norm_inv_le_quarter (s := s₀ - 1) (by simp [hs₀im]) ht
  have hi := norm_inv_le_quarter hsim ht
  have hi' : ‖(s - 1)⁻¹‖ ≤ 1 / 4 := norm_inv_le_quarter (s := s - 1) (by simp [hsim]) ht
  have hΓ := norm_logDeriv_Gammaℝ_le hσ (by linarith) ht
  have hΓ₀ := norm_logDeriv_Gammaℝ_le (σ := 3) (by norm_num) le_rfl ht
  have hC : digammaVerticalLogConstant ≤ 11 := by
    unfold digammaVerticalLogConstant
    have := Real.pi_lt_four
    have := Real.log_two_lt_d9
    linarith
  have hLt := log_ge_of_four_le ht
  -- assemble
  have hxi : logDeriv xi s = logDeriv riemannZeta s₀ + s₀⁻¹ + (s₀ - 1)⁻¹ + logDeriv Gammaℝ s₀
      + ∑' q : XiZeroCopy, ((s - (q.1 : ℂ))⁻¹ - (s₀ - (q.1 : ℂ))⁻¹) := by
    rw [← hpf, hdec₀]; ring
  rw [hdec, hxi]
  have hΓ' : ‖logDeriv Gammaℝ s‖ ≤ Real.log t + digammaVerticalLogConstant := by
    have : ((σ : ℂ) + t * I) = s := rfl
    simpa [this] using hΓ
  have hΓ₀' : ‖logDeriv Gammaℝ s₀‖ ≤ Real.log t + digammaVerticalLogConstant := by
    have : (((3 : ℝ) : ℂ) + t * I) = s₀ := by rw [hs₀def]; push_cast; rfl
    simpa [this] using hΓ₀
  have hLtδ : Real.log t ≤ Real.log t / δ := by
    rw [le_div_iff₀ hδ]
    exact mul_le_of_le_one_right (by linarith) hδ1
  have hK₀ : (0 : ℝ) ≤ smallHeightCount := Nat.cast_nonneg _
  have hK₀' : 0 ≤ 5 * (smallHeightCount : ℝ) * Real.log t / δ := by positivity
  have hfinal : logDerivZetaConstant * Real.log t / δ
      = (3650 + 5 * smallHeightCount) * Real.log t / δ + 50 * (Real.log t / δ) := by
    unfold logDerivZetaConstant; ring
  rw [hfinal]
  calc ‖logDeriv riemannZeta s₀ + s₀⁻¹ + (s₀ - 1)⁻¹ + logDeriv Gammaℝ s₀
        + ∑' q : XiZeroCopy, ((s - (q.1 : ℂ))⁻¹ - (s₀ - (q.1 : ℂ))⁻¹)
        - s⁻¹ - (s - 1)⁻¹ - logDeriv Gammaℝ s‖
      ≤ ‖logDeriv riemannZeta s₀‖ + ‖s₀⁻¹‖ + ‖(s₀ - 1)⁻¹‖ + ‖logDeriv Gammaℝ s₀‖
        + ‖∑' q : XiZeroCopy, ((s - (q.1 : ℂ))⁻¹ - (s₀ - (q.1 : ℂ))⁻¹)‖
        + ‖s⁻¹‖ + ‖(s - 1)⁻¹‖ + ‖logDeriv Gammaℝ s‖ := by
        refine (norm_sub_le _ _).trans ?_
        gcongr
        refine (norm_sub_le _ _).trans ?_
        gcongr
        refine (norm_sub_le _ _).trans ?_
        gcongr
        refine (norm_add_le _ _).trans ?_
        gcongr
        refine (norm_add_le _ _).trans ?_
        gcongr
        refine (norm_add_le _ _).trans ?_
        gcongr

    _ ≤ 2 + 1 / 4 + 1 / 4 + (Real.log t + digammaVerticalLogConstant)
        + (3650 + 5 * smallHeightCount) * Real.log t / δ
        + 1 / 4 + 1 / 4 + (Real.log t + digammaVerticalLogConstant) := by
        gcongr
    _ ≤ (3650 + 5 * smallHeightCount) * Real.log t / δ + 50 * (Real.log t / δ) := by

prose.text:
o needs to know that a hypothetical zero `β+iγ` forces `ζ` to be *small
nearby*: `‖ζ(σ+iγ)‖ ≤ (σ−β)·max‖ζ'‖`.  Without it the lower bound from three-four-one cannot be
contradicted, because nothing connects the value at `σ+iγ` to the zero.

`Sieve/ZetaDerivBound.lean` supplies the derivative half:

- `differentiableOn_riemannZeta_of_ne_one` — `ζ` is differentiable on any set avoiding the pole.
- `norm_deriv_riemannZeta_le` — **Cauchy's estimate**: `‖ζ'(c)‖ ≤ C/R` whenever `‖ζ‖ ≤ C` on the
  circle of radius `R` about `c` and the closed disc avoids `1`.

Unconditional, axioms `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.  With `norm_riemannZeta_strip_le`
supplying `C` on the circle, this bounds `ζ'` throughout the strip.

Still missing: the mean value step from `ζ'` to `ζ` along the segment from the zero.  An attempt
through `Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_hasFDerivWithin_le` foundered on the `ℝ`-versus-`ℂ`
scalar restriction of the derivative; it was removed rather than left broken.  That step, plus the
final optimisation, is what remains.

### The fifth input, completed

`norm_riemannZeta_le_of_zero` (`Sieve/ZetaDerivBound.lean`) — if `ζ(z) = 0`, the segment from `z` to
`c` avoids the pole, and `‖ζ'‖ ≤ M` along it, then

`‖ζ(c)‖ ≤ M·‖c − z‖`.

Unconditional, axioms `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`; printed statement checked.

The earlier attempt failed on the `ℝ`-versus-`ℂ` scalar restriction of `fderiv`.  Parametrising the
segment by a real variable removes the difficulty entirely: `g t = ζ(z + t(c−z))` is a function
`ℝ → ℂ`, the chain rule is `HasDerivAt.scomp`, and the one-dimensional mean value inequality
`Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_hasDerivWithin_le` applies directly on `[0,1]`.

All five inputs of the classical zero-free region are now unconditional in the corpus:

| | |
|---|---|
| three-four-one | `three_four_one_log_zeta_const` |
| real-axis bound `A` | `log_norm_riemannZeta_real_le` |
| strip growth `B` | `norm_riemannZeta_strip_le` |
| derivative bound | `norm_deriv_riemannZeta_le` |
| small near a zero | `norm_riemannZeta_le_of_zero` |

What remains is the optimisation that combines them — choosing the radius, the offset `σ − 1`, and
the constant — to produce a region `σ > 1 − c/log t`.

### The five inputs combined

`Sieve/ZeroFreeCombination.lean`:

- `exp_le_norm_riemannZeta_shift` — for `σ > 1`, given only an upper bound `B₀` at `σ + 2it`,

  `‖ζ(σ+it)‖ ≥ exp((−22 − 3 log(1 + 1/(σ−1)) − log B₀)/4)`.

  An explicit *positive* lower bound off the real axis, from the three-four-one inequality and the
  real-axis bound.
- `le_mul_sub_of_riemannZeta_eq_zero` — a zero at `β + it` gives `‖ζ(σ+it)‖ ≤ M(σ−β)`, hence

  `exp((−22 − 3 log(1 + 1/(σ−1)) − log B₀)/4) ≤ M(σ − β)`.

Unconditional, axioms `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

This is the classical zero-free region argument reduced to a single inequality between explicit
quantities.  The free parameters are the offset `σ − 1`, the derivative bound `M` (from
`norm_deriv_riemannZeta_le` with `norm_riemannZeta_strip_le` on the circle), and `B₀` (from
`norm_riemannZeta_strip_le` at `σ + 2it`); all three grow only logarithmically or linearly in `t`,
so choosing `σ − 1 ≍ 1/log t` yields `β ≤ 1 − c/log t`.

Carrying out that choice — instantiating `M` and `B₀` and doing the calculus — is the remaining
step, and it is now genuinely arithmetic: no further property of `ζ` is required.

### The derivative bound, explicit

`norm_deriv_riemannZeta_le_explicit` (`Sieve/ZetaDerivBound.lean`) — for a disc of radius `R` about
`c` staying in the right half-plane (`R < re c`) and away from the real axis (`R < |im c|`),

`‖ζ'(c)‖ ≤ ((‖c‖ + R)/(|im c| − R) + (‖c‖ + R)/(re c − R))/R`.

Unconditional, axioms `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.  The two geometric hypotheses do
all the work: `R < |im c|` keeps the disc off the real axis, so it avoids the pole *and* gives
`‖w − 1‖ ≥ |im c| − R`; `R < re c` keeps it in the half-plane where the strip bound applies.

This makes the `M` of `le_mul_sub_of_riemannZeta_eq_zero` explicit in terms of the point alone.

**Note on strength.**  With this `M` and with `B₀` from `norm_riemannZeta_strip_le`, both grow
*linearly* in `|t|`, so the resulting region is of the shape `β ≤ 1 − c|t|^{-5/4}` — a genuine
zero-free region, but far weaker than the classical `1 − c/log|t|`.  The classical strength needs
`ζ(σ+it) ≪ log|t|` in the strip, which comes from the truncated Euler–Maclaurin expansion
(`ζ(s) = ∑_{n≤N} n^{-s} + N^{1-s}/(s−1) + O(|s|N^{-σ})` at `N ≍ |t|`), not from the single-term
fractional-part formula used here.  That sharpening is the natural next target.

### Correction — the linear strip bound gives **no** region at all

The note above said the current bounds yield a genuine but weak region `β ≤ 1 − c|t|^{-5/4}`.  That
is wrong; the arithmetic does not close.  Working it through with `σ = 1 + δ`:

ted formula:
`Sieve/ZetaTruncated.riemannZeta_eq_sum_add_tail` gives, for `re w > 0`, `w != 1`, `N >= 1`,

```text
zeta(w) = sum_{k <= N} k^(-w) + N^(1-w)/(w-1) - w * int_N^inf fract(x) x^(-w-1) dx.
```

What was missing is that the existing bound `norm_riemannZeta_le_truncated` immediately applies
`norm_sum_le` to the head, replacing the complex sum by the sum of moduli — **which discards all
cancellation and can only ever give the trivial logarithmic size**. The whole point of the Z3 chain
is a bound on the oscillating sum, so the head must survive as a complex sum.

Added:

- `norm_riemannZeta_le_partialSum` : the same identity bounded one step earlier —

  ```text
  ‖zeta(w)‖ <= ‖sum_{k <= N} k^(-w)‖ + N^(1-re w)/‖w-1‖ + ‖w‖*(N^(-re w)/re w).
  ```

- `norm_riemannZeta_one_add_I_mul_le` : on the line, for `t > 0` and `N >= 1`,

  ```text
  ‖zeta(1+It)‖ <= ‖sum_{k <= N} k^(-(1+It))‖ + 1/t + ‖1+It‖/N.
  ```

The two tail terms are harmless at the Z3 truncation point: with `N = 2^(topExponent t + 1) - 1`,
`N ~ 2*(t/8pi)^3`, so `‖1+It‖/N ~ t/N ~ 0` and `1/t -> 0`. `Finset.Icc 1 N = Finset.Ico 1 (N+1)`
matches the Z3 range exactly.

Z4 is therefore reduced to a cast/index reconciliation plus these two vanishing terms.

## Z4 index/cast bridge (2026-08-06)

`formal/GaloisForLFunctions/RHTower/Sieve/ZetaLineIndexBridge.lean` — built, wired, axioms
`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, zero warnings.

- `sum_Icc_cpow_eq_sum_Ico` : the truncation's head and the derivative test's range are the same
  sum,

  ```text
  sum_{k in Icc 1 M} ((k:R):C)^(-(1+It)) = sum_{n in Ico 1 (M+1)} (n:C)^(-1-It).
  ```

  (`Finset.Ico_add_one_right_eq_Icc` for the range; base cast and exponent rearrangement termwise.)

- `cube_le_two_pow_topExponent` : the chain's truncation point is large,

  ```text
  8*pi <= t  ==>  (t/(8*pi))^3 <= 2^(topExponent t + 1).
  ```

  (`Nat.lt_floor_add_one` on the definition of `topExponent`, then compare exponentials.)

Together these close the two mismatches identified when Z4 was opened. With
`M + 1 = 2^(topExponent t + 1)` the truncation reads

```text
‖zeta(1+It)‖ <= ‖sum_{n in Ico 1 (2^(topExponent t + 1))} n^(-1-It)‖ + 1/t + ‖1+It‖/M,
```

whose head is exactly what `littlewood_littleOh` bounds, and whose last term is at most
`(1+t)/((t/8pi)^3 - 1)`, which tends to 0. The remaining step is to assemble these into a statement
about `zeta(1+It)` itself.

## Z4 closed: a bound on zeta(1+It) itself (2026-08-06)

`formal/GaloisForLFunctions/RHTower/Sieve/ZetaLineLittleOh.lean` — built, wired, axioms
`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, zero warnings.

```text
lineTruncation t := 2^(topExponent t + 1) - 1

norm_riemannZeta_line_littleOh (heps : 0 < eps) :
  exists T, forall t >= T,
    ‖zeta(1 + It)‖ <= 1 + log 2 + eps*log(t/2pi) + 1/t + (1+t)/((t/(8pi))^3 - 1).
```

The head is the derivative-test bound transported through the truncation; the two tail terms are
explicit and both tend to 0 (the second because the chain's truncation point grows like the **cube**
of `t` while `‖1+It‖` grows linearly — an enormous margin, not a delicate one).

**This is a bound on `zeta` itself, not on a partial sum**, and it is unconditional. Together with
`cube_sub_one_le_lineTruncation` and the index bridge, the Z3+Z4 chain now runs from the k-th
derivative test to the qualitative statement

```text
zeta(1 + It) = o(log t).
```

Remaining on the card: the quantitative exponent (`K` growing with `t`, giving
`O(log t/loglog t)`), and Z5 (the rectangle `sigma`-version, which reuses `abel_block_bound` with
`w n = n^(-sigma)`). The Landau/3-4-1 pipeline in `PNTPlus/ZetaBounds` then consumes the rectangle
version to produce the zero-free region.

## Z5 opened: the block bound off the line (2026-08-06)

`formal/GaloisForLFunctions/RHTower/Sieve/DirichletBlockSigma.lean` — built, wired, axioms
`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, zero warnings.

`dirichlet_block_sigma_bound` : for `sigma >= 0`, `1 <= N <= M`, and any prefix bound `P` on the
pure phase sum,

```text
(forall m in [N,M], ‖sum_{Ico N m} n^(-It)‖ <= P)
  ==>  ‖sum_{Ico N M} n^(-sigma-It)‖ <= P * N^(-sigma).
```

This is the exact analogue of `dirichlet_block_one_bound`, and the proof is the same Abel step with
`w n = n^(-sigma)` in place of `n^(-1)`: the weight is antitone for `sigma >= 0` and nonnegative, so

**Nothing in the derivative test changes.** The `k`-th derivative test controls the pure phase sum

whole Z3 chain is `sigma`-independent up to the final Abel step, and the rectangle version costs
only this substitution plus re-running the assembly with `N^(-sigma)` in place of `N^(-1)`.

Next: the `sigma`-analogue of `dirichlet_block_one_full` (same prefix bound from
